metadata.title: Forest productivity vulnerability to climate and forest loss
metadata.description: The study asked where climate stress and forest loss are weakening humid tropical forests. It found widespread vulnerability of forest productivity in the Amazon, with stronger signals along the arc of deforestation. This 0.1-degree map is the dimensionless diagnostic index for gross primary productivity. Negative values indicate vulnerability toward lower productivity; positive values toward higher productivity, and values near zero indicate relative stability. In-shade heat stress: historical climate with retained Amazon forest
metadata.description: The study used a climate model to ask how complete replacement of Amazon forest by savanna would change heat stress alongside global warming. Across paired simulations, savannization raised in-shade heat stress, with greater increases under RCP8.5. This file supplies the historical climate (1981-2010) scenario with retained Amazon forest. metadata.citation: ter Steege et al. (2023). Mapping density, diversity and species-richness of the Amazon tree flora. Version2. Figshare. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.22786166.v2
metadata.study_time: April 2023 ATDN compilation; the underlying plot census dates vary and do not establish one map observation interval.

publications.title: Mapping density, diversity and species-richness of the Amazon tree flora

limitations: Based on old-growth forest plots and interpolated over the original lowland forest extent; this is not a current forest-cover inventory.
annotations.temporal_note: Catalog time is the source-file modification date, not a measurement date.
annotations.processing: Original ASCII grid preserved byte for byte; no spatial reference or geometry assigned.

annotations.meaning: Estimated species richness per hectare
annotations.tree_definition: Free-standing woody individuals with diameter at breast height at least 10 cm.
